echo keeps a rolling history of recent audio. Older audio is replaced as the history fills. Save a clip to keep it in your Library.

Choose how far back to save. SAVE CLIP keeps that audio up to the moment you tap it. It does not start a timed recording.

Save new audio from now on as successive Library clips. Turning this off saves the final short clip. Clip interval and retention are in Settings → Saving clips.
Saved changes will apply the next time recording starts. Your current audio history is unchanged.

Maximum %1$d MB on this device. This is compressed audio history, not the whole app. Saving can temporarily reserve the same amount again.
Use a larger temporary history on device storage. This still replaces old audio; it does not keep permanent clips.
16–1024 MB total. Half holds recent audio and half is reserved while a clip is being saved.
Higher quality uses more memory and storage.
History is compressed as Opus. WAV and FLAC cannot recover quality already lost.
FLAC · lossless export of decoded history
Save clips automatically in every session
While recording, save new audio to Library at the interval below. This choice persists across sessions.
Save before new audio uses 75% of the rolling history budget. Applies to automatic saves and Keep this session in clips.
Target length of each automatic or session clip, from 10 to 3600 seconds. 300 means 5 minutes. Choose less than the available history, or enable early saving.
Automatic clips to keep in each group
Keep 1–500 clips in each automatic or session group. New clips replace the oldest after this limit. Clips saved with SAVE CLIP stay until you delete them.
Recording pauses outside this window. Overnight windows work; matching times mean all day.
Set 0% to disable. Recording resumes when the battery recovers.
Android may delay schedule changes without exact-alarm access. After a reboot, open echo to resume recording.
Saved recordings always stay in echo. A chosen folder receives a verified additional copy. Renaming, deleting and automatic retention in echo do not change those copies.
Could not access that folder. Choose another one.
Other apps can control recording through echo’s documented intents. Android may require opening echo before starting the microphone.
One-time English model download: about 40 MB. Used for offline transcription and spoken camera commands. Speech detection needs no download. Vosk 0.15 · Apache 2.0.
The download failed. Check your connection and try again.
The model could not load. Try stopping and restarting recording.
While microphone recording is running, say the complete command below. echo then records video with sound for the chosen duration. Commands are ignored while a camera clip is recording or saving.

Saves a screenshot once a minute while the screen is active. Android asks for screen-sharing permission each session. Protected content may be hidden. Screenshots cannot run at the same time as device-audio capture.
Start recording from Record before using this action.
Switching starts a new audio history. Saved recordings stay in Library. Device audio works only with apps that allow audio capture.

Rolling history is temporary. When its budget fills, the oldest audio is replaced. SAVE CLIP copies recent audio to Library so it stays there. Starting a new recording or closing the app process clears unsaved history.

Recording first builds temporary rolling history. You can save recent audio by hand, keep new audio for this session from Record, or enable automatic clips for every session here. All saved clips appear in Library.
Choose what echo processes after saving an audio clip. Manual controls are available in each clip.
Automatically find speech in new clips
Mark detected speech on the waveform and label the clip in Library. Existing clips are unchanged.
Generate English text after each new clip is saved. Also marks speech. Download the English model below before enabling this.
Processing stays on this device and may use extra battery and memory. Transcripts can contain mistakes. Automatic options apply to newly saved audio clips.
Enter a complete English phrase. Each camera needs a different phrase; one cannot contain the other.
Use a distinct English phrase of 3–100 characters. Letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens are supported.
Record 5–600 seconds after a command. Default: 30 seconds. Both cameras use this duration.
Switch the audio source to Microphone to use camera commands.
Android reports front and back cameras. If a camera cannot start, audio recording continues.
Back camera only. Front-camera commands are unavailable on this device.
Front camera only. Back-camera commands are unavailable on this device.
No video camera is available. Audio recording and analysis still work.
Drag to seek. Pinch or use buttons to zoom. Waveform height shows relative volume.
Speech has not been analyzed yet.
No speech detected. Quiet or unclear speech may be missed.
%1$s of speech detected · Green bands mark speech on the waveform.
Tap a word to seek to it. Automatically generated English text may contain mistakes.
No transcript yet. Choose TRANSCRIBE to create one.
No words were recognized. This does not guarantee that the clip contains no speech.
Audio that SAVE CLIP will keep. The graph fits your selected duration as history fills.
Amplitude history for the last %1$s of the clip available to save
Another app has an active microphone recording. Starting echo may silence that app, or echo may receive no audio. Stop the other recording first, or continue.
A call or voice-chat audio session is active. It may take microphone priority over echo. End it first, or continue.
Android could not report other microphone use. If another app is recording, starting echo may interrupt it or receive no audio. Continue?

Starting this can stop another app’s screen sharing or system-audio capture, including a visualizer. Android does not reliably let echo check whether one is active. Stop the other capture first, or continue. Android will ask for screen-sharing permission next.
